transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18 15:00 PT | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Bluehaven Sr. ML Eng), Rafael Ortiz (Bluehaven Head of Platform), Priya Kapoor (Bluehaven SecOps)

Summary (auto): quick retrospective of pilot week 3, infra gating items, security handoff, and agreement on next-step benchmarks. Focus on access, SSO, KMS integration, and a short perf retest with quantized model.
Topics: onboarding progress, credentialing, VPC peering, KMS flow, latency vs batch tuning, fallback plan to hosted.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off real quick — this is the week 3 onboarding readiness and ops debrief. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Rafael: Rafael here.
[00:10] Maya: Maya on — sorry had to mute for a sec.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, good afternoon.
[00:14] Arjun: Arjun here.
[00:16] Sofia: Great. Big items: we wanted to confirm staging access, SSO test, and the plan for the perf rerun using the quant profile we discussed last call. Any blockers to start?
[00:28] Maya: Blocking for me is the lack of peered VPC network — we can't route to your staging endpoint unless Rafael's team opens the peering and assigns the subnets. We got the temporary creds but the CIDR blocks overlap with one of our on-prem ranges.
[00:40] Rafael: Yeah, we found that after I spun up the staging environment. We'll need to adjust. We're opening an infra ticket but wanted to know if Redwood can accept a different subnet mask or if we should route via NAT.
[00:52] Arjun: We can support either but NAT adds egress hops and might add 30-80ms under load, so for latency-sensitive paths we prefer peering. Also, we can run through a short smoke test via the public gateway to validate credentials before peering is finalized.
[01:08] Priya: From SecOps, the bigger ask is KMS integration — our policy requires that keys are never exported and that we maintain access logs for a minimum of 2 years. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[01:20] Sofia: Short answer: yes, we support a customer-managed KMS workflow in both Dedicated and Private modes. For Hosted there's a bring-your-own-key option with HSM-backed KMS — though our hosted plane stores only token-level metadata, we can provide audit logs on request.
[01:34] Maya: There's a doc mismatch — I looked at "Redwood Private" guide and a section says "key rotation handled by Redwood" which would be a hard no for Priya's team.
[01:42] Sofia: Noted. We'll send the updated private deployment KMS section. That doc may be from older copy; private deployments absolutely let you control the master CMK in the cloud KMS or HSM. We'll attach the SOC2 encryption appendix.
[01:56] Rafael: Also curious about SSO / SAML. We run Okta with SCIM. Will SCIM provisioning be necessary for user-level RBAC?
[02:06] Arjun: We integrate with SAML SSO for auth and support SCIM for provisioning users and groups. Role-based access maps to our platform roles (viewer, operator, admin). There can be some mapping quirks — for example, group names with spaces sometimes get transformed.
[02:20] Priya: Keep that note — our naming conv is pretty strict. Also, we need to validate audit log retention — is that configurable per-tenant or global?
[02:29] Sofia: Per-tenant retention is an enterprise add-on; default retention is 60 days on hosted, but Dedicated/Private customers can request longer retention. We'll list options in the follow-up.
[02:40] Maya: Moving to performance: Arjun, on our last run we saw tail latency spikes when the batcher ramped above 12 requests. We suspected the KV cache hits weren't lining up with our prompt prefix distribution. Can you explain how Redwood's cache strategy works in the runtime?
[02:56] Arjun: Sure — our runtime uses prefix-aware KV caching plus request coalescing. If the prompt prefix matches cached KV segments we bypass recompute. But if you have lots of high-variance prefixes (like unique user ids in prompt), cache hit rate drops. For the POC, we recommended a prompt canonicalization step to improve alignment. Also we pushed a quantized variant for lower memory footprints which changes kernel selection and can affect latency distribution.
[03:20] Maya: Right, we ran the quantized model and saw lower average latency but occasionally higher 95th percentile — maybe due to CPU fallbacks?
[03:28] Arjun: That's possible. Quantized execution paths sometimes trigger alternative kernels when sequence lengths change mid-stream. We'll run a small synthetic with varying sequence lengths to reproduce.
[03:36] Rafael: Is there a way to prefer lower p95 at cost of higher average tokens cost? That's what the product team is asking.
[03:44] Sofia: Yes — you can tune batch size, max latency targets, and prefer a model variant. We can set an aggressive batching policy for throughput in Dedicated or pin an unquantized variant for low tail latency in Private deployments. It's a tradeoff.
[03:56] Priya: Any fallback if staging hits capacity? We want predictable behavior for prod cutover.
[04:02] Arjun: We support smart routing: fallback from low-cost quantized nodes to a higher-SLA unquantized pool. Route policy is configurable per-route. For pilot we'll recommend an automatic fallback plus alerting hooks so Bluehaven gets paged before degradation impacts surface-level users.
[04:18] Sofia: OK small operational asks — Maya: can you share the 100-sample prompt set you mentioned? We'll use that for the next bench.
[04:26] Maya: Yes, I'll upload it to the shared drive after this call. It has a mix of short and long contexts, and a few structured JSON responses we expect to parse.
[04:34] Maya (later garbled): ...and there's a couple of prompts that include user IDs, so we do want to try canonicalization.
[04:42] Arjun: Good — we'll run two bench variants: with canonicalization and without. We'll also run a quantized-unquantized comparison at 10k requests.
[04:52] Sofia: Rafael, on peering, can your infra team confirm an alternate CIDR we can accept? We can also open a temporary public gateway for smoke tests if needed.
[05:00] Rafael: I'll check. We may be able to allocate a /20 that doesn't overlap. If that's tight, NAT is the fallback.
[05:06] Priya: On compliance — we need to validate that firewall logs and audit trails can be exported to our SIEM. Does Redwood push logs to an S3-like bucket or do you offer syslog?
[05:18] Arjun: We can stream audit logs to a customer-managed S3 or to syslog endpoints for Dedicated/Private, or via a hosted log exporter for Hosted customers. We'll include example retention and export config in the doc bundle.
[05:30] Priya: Good. Also, data residency — we have EU customers whose data must remain in EU regions. For the hosted option can you pin region?
[05:40] Sofia: Hosted supports region pinning per-tenant; we have EU regions available. For Dedicated/Private you control region fully.
[05:46] Maya: Timeline check — we want to get a bench run and a preliminary pass on security by next Thursday. Is that realistic?
[05:54] Sofia: Yes, assuming peering or gateway is done this week.
[05:58] Arjun: I'll run the synthetic and post the perf sheet by Wed/Thu. If we hit peering delays we'll do gateway smoke and then full run once peering is in place.
[06:08] Sofia: Alright let's do a quick retro: what went well, what tripped us, and what to fix for the handoff to ops.
[06:14] Rafael: Went well: quick turnaround on staging images and the initial config. Tripped: CIDR overlap and credential rotation timing between teams. Fix: standardized provisioning doc and a shared inventory for subnets.
[06:26] Maya: Went well: quant profile reduced avg cost. Tripped: p95 spikes and canonicalization not applied early enough. Fix: integrate prompt canonicalization in our ingestion lane before calling the API.
[06:38] Priya: Went well: we have a clear KMS requirement. Tripped: doc mismatch on key rotation. Fix: Redwood to send the private deployment KMS appendix and example policies.
[06:50] Sofia: Great. We'll also add a short runbook for fallback: if peering fails, enable NAT smoke tests and schedule the full perf for when peering is established.
[06:58] Arjun: One technical note — when we run the quantized bench I'll include a column for kernel fallback counts; that should help correlate p95 spikes.
[07:06] Maya: Perfect. Also please include the telemetry keys and sample spans so our tracing team can map traces to Redwood request ids.
[07:14] Arjun: Will do — we'll provide trace hook examples and the span naming convention.
[07:20] Sofia: Any other open questions?
[07:24] Priya: Just one: do you support customer-managed HSMs for on-prem private installs or only cloud KMS?
[07:32] Arjun: For on-prem Private we can integrate with customer HSMs — we did a similar integration for a bank last year. We'll surface the architecture diagram in the doc pack.
[07:42] Rafael: Good. That covers most.
[07:46] Sofia: Ok closure: reiterate next steps - we'll send updated docs (KMS appendix, SSO mapping notes, staging network diagram), Arjun runs perf and posts CSV, Bluehaven provisions peering or opens NAT gateway, Maya uploads prompt set, Priya sends compliance Qs.
[07:58] Maya: I'll upload the prompt set today.
[08:02] Priya: I'll compile the compliance list and send it by Monday.
[08:06] Rafael: I'll open the ticket and confirm a non-overlapping CIDR by tomorrow.
[08:12] Sofia: Fantastic. I'll share the doc bundle and a shortened runbook. Thanks everyone.
[08:18] (meeting ends)
